memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And the Lord said to Moses, 'I will do the very thing you have asked, because I am pleased with you and I know you by name.'" - Exod 33:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God grants the request. And He gives His reason: "I know you by name."

That phrase is not a formality. In Scripture, to be known by name is to be known personally, individually, particularly. God is not managing humanity as a crowd. He knows Moses — this man, with this history, these fears, this stammer, this past failure in Egypt.

We can lose sight of this. Among billions of people, prayer can feel like shouting into a vast hall. But Jesus said the Good Shepherd calls His own sheep by name (John 10:3), and that He knows them and they know Him (John 10:14). Not by number. By name.

We must be careful, though, not to twist this into a formula: God did not grant the request because Moses had earned leverage. God's favour rested on Moses as a gift, and Moses' bold prayer flowed out of that favour, not the other way round.

That is exactly our position in Christ. We do not pray to gain God's acceptance; we pray from it. Our confidence in asking rests on the fact that we are already known, already loved, already His.

God knows your name too. Not your role, not your usefulness. You.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God knows you personally, or only generally?
2. How does being known by God change how you pray?
3. Are you praying to earn God's favour, or from it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You know me by name. I come to You not to win Your love but because I already have it in Christ. Amen.
